subject: Dedicated cluster throughput degradation — coordinated remediation & credit proposal
messages:
From: Aria Patel <aria.patel@orbital.ai>

Cc: ops@orbital.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden throughput drop on dedicated pool in us-west-2

Hi Jonas team,

We started seeing a steady increase in latency and a drop in throughput for our booked dedicated pool in us-west-2 starting ~08:45 PDT. This has caused timeouts in our inference pipeline — we're observing ~30% fewer completions per minute and late tails at ~4s per token rather than the expected ~1s.

Impact: customer-facing feature degradation for ~30% of requests. We're on a tight launch window and this is blocking our rollout.

Can you confirm whether this is a known issue with the dedicated pools? We've attached a short trace and the request IDs we could grab.

Attachments: orbital_trace_20260402.txt (text, 18KB)

Thanks,
Aria
Sr. Platform Engineer
Orbital.AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden throughput drop on dedicated pool in us-west-2

Quick triage notes (internal):
- Observed saturating async executor queues on tenant pool gw-ded-37 (us-west-2).
- Backpressure likely caused by a combination of increased long-context requests and an autoscaler cooldown that recently changed (policy v2.3) — verified by spike in warmup latency at 08:43.
- No kernel rollout at 08:40; last kernel change was 04/01 23:10.
- Evictions increased 4x for tenants sharing that pool starting 08:41.

Immediate mitigations applied at 10:05:
1) Temporarily opened burst capacity (added two warm nodes to pool gw-ded-37).
2) Increased autoscaler sensitivity for the pool for the next 2 hours.
3) Applied routing rule to move Orbital.AI traffic to gw-ded-42 (same AZ) with graceful KV cache warm transfer.

I'll continue to monitor and will push a follow-up with diagnostics (heap, GPU util, queue depth) and a recommended long-term fix.

Marissa
Sr. Operations Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rbw_diagnostics_v1.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Aria Patel <aria.patel@orbital.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 04 Apr 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Dedicated cluster throughput degradation — coordinated remediation & credit proposal

Hi Aria — long update and next steps below. Apologies again for the disruption over Friday morning.

What happened (summary):
- Root cause: sustained burst of long-context requests from multiple tenants saturated the async executor queue on gw-ded-37. The autoscaler cooldown parameter introduced in v2.3 delayed node replenishment, and our KV warm transfer was slower than expected for that pool, which amplified tail latency for tenants sharing the pool.
- Impact window: 2026-04-02 08:41 - 2026-04-02 10:10 PDT. Orbital.AI experienced ~30% throughput degradation and elevated per-token latency during the window.

Actions taken (remediation):
- Immediate: opened burst capacity and routed Orbital.AI to a warmed sibling pool (gw-ded-42) at 10:05 — this restored expected throughput within ~4 minutes.
- Short-term (applied): reverted the autoscaler cooldown change for the affected pools, tuned queue backpressure thresholds, and added a KV pre-warm step for routing switchovers.
- Long-term (planned): implement workload-aware autoscaler profiles that detect long-context request patterns per-tenant and reserve ephemeral warm nodes; add aKV transfer optimization to avoid tail warm penalties. ETA: incremental rollout starting 2026-04-20.

Customer remedy and credits:
- We will provide Orbital.AI a service credit equal to 10% of April dedicated usage (applied as account credit) to offset the impact on your launch window. Details in attached credit_calculation_sheet.xlsx.
- We're offering a short technical session with our infra team to review workload tuning (30–45 minutes) at your convenience.

Follow-up items we own:
- Post-incident diagnostic packet (attached rbw_diagnostics_v1.pdf).
- Implementation plan for autoscaler profile + pre-warm transfer (share design by 2026-04-10).
- Schedule review call — Marissa/Ben/Jonas available next week between 10am–3pm PT. Please share a couple slots that work for you.

If you prefer a redacted incident timeline and root-cause writeup suitable for your internal audit, we can produce that as well.

Thanks for your patience — we value Orbital's partnership and want to make sure this doesn't recur.

Jonas Weber
Principal Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): rbw_diagnostics_v1.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB); credit_calculation_sheet.xlsx (xlsx, 32KB)
